Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to move faster on contracting so we can finalize the PO. Our legal team attached a marked-up DPA (helix-dpa-redlines.pdf) and a short note on transfer-impact items they want clarified — primarily:

- Retention and export controls for EU-origin data (TIA requests).

Appreciate a quick alignment call if helpful — Tom / Contracts can do 10–11am PT tomorrow.

Thanks,

Tom — thanks for the package and the clear priorities. I reviewed the PDF and sketched an execution plan below. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Proposed approach (2-track):
1) Legal redline triage (priority):
   - We’ll take the Helix redlines and produce a response redline of the DPA and MSA cross-references.
   - Focus first on SCCs selection, controller/processor mapping, and subprocessors clause.
   - Deliverable: redwood_dpa_response_v1.docx by EOD tomorrow.
2) Technical evidence / TIA scope (parallel):
   - Laura + infra will produce a short TIA-risk-matrix.xlsx describing where data is stored, retention, and export controls for EU-origin requests.
   - Deliverable: TIA-risk-matrix.xlsx within 48 hours.

Key asks from Helix to unblock:
- Confirm whether Helix requires Module Two (processor-to-controller) SCCs or Module Three (controller-to-processor) as currently redlined.
- Whether Helix needs an up-to-date list of subprocessors before signature or if a rolling notification is acceptable.

Action items:
- I will draft and share redline (Attachment: redwood_dpa_response_v1.docx).
- Karthik, can you do a legal pass focused on SCCs + Appendix language?
- Laura, please draft the TIA matrix and short privacy opinion.
- David, FYI for procurement / PO timing.

Tom — if that timeline works I’ll send the redline and we can iterate during tomorrow’s call.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + TIA questions (MSA/Order Form)

Thanks Priya — quick legal notes after a first pass of redwood_dpa_response_v1.docx: 

- SCCs: Helix’s redline looks like Module Three language. Our standard position (given Redwood acts as processor) is to accept the EU Commission SCCs for controller-processor transfers (Module Two/Controller-to-Processor) with an Annex describing subprocessors and transfer routes. If Helix insists on Module Three, we need to confirm why (it’s atypical when customer is controller).

- Roles & logging: Recommended explicit text that customer (Helix) is controller for model outputs and customer data; Redwood remains processor for request payloads and telemetry. Add explicit exceptions for aggregated telemetry used for system performance (pseudonymous).

- Retention/extracts: Push to reasonable caps + customer-triggered export process (30-calendar-day notice for export requests). Avoid open-ended export rights that force engineering heavy lift.

- Subprocessors: We should offer: (a) current subprocessors list in Annex 1, (b) rolling notification for future subprocessors, (c) right to object for Helix on narrow security grounds with 30-day cure period.

- Export controls / TIA: Recommend pairing a short technical Annex (TIA matrix) with the legal language so procurement/legal can see evidence. Laura — can you confirm the minimal evidence set (region, AES keys, KMS, HSM usage) so infra can prepare?

I’ll mark up redwood_dpa_response_v1.docx with inline comments and a short redline regarding SCC selection.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, david_kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + TIA questions (MSA/Order Form)

Following up with the privacy opinion and TIA checklist:

Summary (privacy-opinion-summary.txt attached):
- Accept SCCs Annex with controller-processor orientation. We should provide Helix with: (1) Annex listing current subprocessors and locations, (2) TIA matrix with data flow for EU-origin requests, and (3) a bounded data retention schedule mapped to feature sets.
- For transfer-impact addendum (TIA): keep it scoped to EU-origin operational data only (avoid committing to model weights or aggregated research outputs). This reduces product risk.
- Suggest a target execution timeline: legal redline exchange < 48 hours, final DPA sign-off within 5 business days after agreement on SCCs module and Annex.

Technical evidence items for infra (short list to hand to engineering):
- Hosting regions for production and backups (primary region + failover)
- KMS details (provider, AES key rotations, HSM if used)
- Log retention windows by log type (request logs, system logs, aggregate telemetry)
- Subprocessor names and relevant SOC2 / ISO attestations

I’ve attached a short privacy opinion text file and will coordinate with infra to produce the TIA-risk-matrix.xlsx entries.

Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: privacy-opinion-summary.txt
